text: A beautifully configured calendar is still useless until a period is actually open. This lesson closes chapter four with period statuses, and the steps around opening a ledger's very first period.

Every period carries one of five statuses: Never Opened, Future Enterable for posting ahead of schedule, Open for normal activity, Closed but reopenable, and Permanently Closed, which can never be reopened.
Periods generally move left to right through these statuses over their lifetime — never opened, then open, closed at month-end, and eventually permanently closed once audits are complete.

Before opening the first period, the whole chapter's work needs to be in place: the calendar assigned, the ledger created with its chart of accounts and currency, and at least one legal entity assigned.
Period status isn't a one-time setup step — it's actively managed every accounting cycle. That completes chapter four. Chapter five turns to the chart of accounts itself.
